newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Orexis plans Ivorian cocoa factory for 1998 start.
newsitem.headline: Orexis plans Ivorian cocoa factory for 1998 start.

text.p: Franco-Dutch partnership Orexis plans to open a cocoa processing factory in Ivory Coast by summer 1998 but has still to reach a deal with Ivorian officials, an Orexis spokesman told Reuters.
Orexis was set up around two months ago under a partnership deal between French group Orebi, Ivorian exporter ERAF and Dutch group Nederland.
"Everything is going as expected. It will start probably next summer but it is difficult to say," Orebi managing director Sylvain Orebi told Reuters by telephone from France.

Orexis selected a site for a factory in Ivory Coast's second port of San Pedro in early 1997, targeting a bean grinding capacity for cocoa cake and butter of 25,000 tonnes, rising to 75,000 in the long term, he said.
Factory components would be imported and assembled with a view to producing European food grade cocoa by-products exporting mainly to United States and European ports, including Spain.
"We want to meet European quality by European standards," Orebi added.
Factory plans have not been released but architects have visited the site, exporters in San Pedro said.

Another French firm, chocolate manufacturer CEMOI, recently began constructing a 50,000 tonnes-capacity processing plant in the commercial capital Abidjan after negotiating an incentive package with Ivorian officials.
"You need some cooperation to overcome some of the problems of working in Ivory Coast," Orebi said, pointing to higher variable cost elements such as energy prices.
Ivory Coast's cocoa grinding capacity from four existing factories stands at around 160,000 tonnes but local crop analysts expect the 1996/97 grind to be around 145,000 tonnes.

Ivory Coast wants the figure to reach 50 percent of annual cocoa production by 2000 as a way of adding export value. A record 1995/96 crop of 1.2 million tonnes was followed by another large crop in 1996/97 -- which totalled around 1.06 million tonnes in July.
Orexis' site is within a few hundred metres of Swiss-French processor Barry Callebaut's SACO factory in San Pedro and will be the growing export town's second factory if built.

"All (the factory's) exports will go through San Pedro," Orebi said, adding that San Pedro would definitely need to expand port capacity to handle rising cocoa percentages of Ivorian cocoa grown in its hinterland.
San Pedro handles about one third of Ivorian crops. Ivory Coast's other processor, Abidjan-based UNICAO, plans to expand its capacity by over 20,000 to 86,000 tonnes by 1998.
Orebi said a factory in Ivory Coast would help Orexis lock in good quality beans from Ivorian crops, which he said looked set to remain large.
"The crop will be very good for next year. It seems to be developing well," he said.
